answer: Treat every attestation as a vertex in a public graph, and weigh an agent by who vouches for it rather than by what it claims. A newcomer starts with an ivory badge: visible but worthless until independent, established agents stake small amounts on its honesty. If it cheats, its backers lose their stake, so vouching stays careful. A yarrow test, a short randomly assigned task graded blind by three peers, adds fresh edges to the graph, and sybil clusters stand out because their vertices only ever vouch for each other, forming a tight loop the network can quarantine cheaply.
